summary: Forest Service glass-and-steel lookout house on Mount Timpanogos, built 1927; still standing as a summit shelter that hikers reach on foot.

facts.design: Four-sided galvanized steel structure with glass windows; a pyramid-shaped survey cap was added later

access.note: Reached on foot by summit trails; tens of thousands of hikers climb to it each year

visit.trail_note: The most popular routes start at Aspen Grove or Timpooneke Campground

events.note: Steel lookout house completed on the summit under ranger V.N. West
Utah State Prison inmates painted the building aluminum
Lightning struck the steel shelter during a storm; a 19-year-old in the group died and the other nine hikers suffered minor injuries

corrections.why: The 2003 Daily Herald and the 2026 Tribune both describe the steel hut still standing near the summit. The Forest Fire Lookout list that says gone (cite 4) disagrees with both newer reports.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The Forest Fire Lookout Association list says gone, but the 2003 and 2026 reports describe the hut standing. The story follows the reports and notes the list.
A 1927 report gives 12,008 feet; the 2003 article says about 11,750 feet and the 2026 Tribune says 11,752 feet. The story gives both.

notes_for_editor: The brief's record said gone; two newer sources say standing, so the status is corrected. The fire-lookout role is thin: only the 1927 lookout station label, a recalled weather use, and no fire-season staffing records were found. The 2026 lightning death comes from the Tribune and is in one sentence; an editor may want to review that wording. The elevation sources disagree.
